page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.r6a.xlarge is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance configured with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. Powered by an AMD EPYC 7H12 processor running at 2.6 GHz on the x86_64 architecture, this KVM-hypervised instance features 4 physical cores with 1.0 thread per core. The CPU cache configuration includes 32 KB of L1d cache, 0.5 MB of L2 cache, and 16 MB of L3 cache. It does not include local storage or GPU accelerators, and it provides a baseline network bandwidth of 2 Gbps.

Benchmark evaluations indicate that the ecs.r6a.xlarge exhibits modest processing capabilities. Its single-core and multi-core CPU performance in stress-ng tests falls into the bottom 10%, and its multi-threaded bzip3 decompression is similarly positioned. Geekbench results show average single-core performance in the middle 50% but weak multi-core performance in the bottom 25%, which is also reflected in software compilation, ray tracing, and image processing tests. Memory bandwidth tests for both small and large blocks are categorized as weak, though the PassMark memory score and CPU encryption tests achieve average ratings.

The primary tradeoff of the ecs.r6a.xlarge is its high memory capacity relative to its lower-tier processing speeds and lack of local storage. While the 32.0 GB RAM allocation supports memory-intensive operations, the underlying AMD EPYC 7H12 processor limits its suitability for compute-heavy tasks. Consequently, this instance is best suited for memory-bound workloads that do not require high CPU throughput, such as caching layers, medium-sized databases with low transaction volumes, and lightweight enterprise applications.

Built on the x86_64 architecture with KVM virtualization, it offers a high memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core but lacks local storage and GPU acceleration. Benchmark data reveals modest processing capabilities, with stress-ng CPU performance in the bottom 10% and weak multi-core Geekbench scores, though single-core Geekbench and PassMark memory scores reach average levels. The instance features a 16 MB L3 cache and supports AES and SHA cryptography instructions.
